chunks: And certainly We revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate (anyone with God), your deeds will surely become void, and you will surely be among the losers.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a prophet's deeds if they commit shirk according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the infallibility (Ismah) of the Prophets, as the conditional 'if' implies the possibility of shirk to prove that their actual deeds were never nullified. It underscores that divine revelation to Muhammad and previous prophets carried the same core warning against polytheism, reinforcing the continuity of the message of Tawhid. This serves as a theological proof that the Prophets were protected from major sins, ensuring the validity of their intercession and guidance.
